## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

# T-074  An alias or a rename rests on the latest adjudication of its observation

_One task, one pull request. Read `CLAUDE.md` first; beyond it this file is self-contained. Index, order and the owner decision register: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md`. Source: `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/OPEN-ITEMS-PLAN.md` row OI-57, item (6) (`grep -n -F '(6) `db._names_term`' workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/OPEN-ITEMS-PLAN.md`), found by the author of T-069 (`grep -n -F 'Chosen (authoring 2026-11-13): the latest adjudication governs' workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-069-promote-adjudicated-observations.md`). Every number in this file was read on 2026-11-13 on commit `66a5ba8a` and is given with the command that produces it: re-run the command; do not trust the number._

**Pilot status.** Not piloted. Authored 2026-11-13 (Opus-class plan integrator). The defect was reproduced on a scratch copy (section 3); no fix was prototyped. Expect to find a defect in this file, and report it rather than work around it.

## 1. Identity

## 2. Preconditions

- **The integration base.** `origin/main` once the workplan's pull request is merged, otherwise the remote branch carrying the newest commit to this folder (the set-up block's first line finds it).
- **Tasks that must be merged to the integration base first:** none. Check by running: nothing to check. (T-069 should run after this task; that edge belongs to T-069's file, not to this one.)
- **Owner decisions:** none.
- **Tests that must be red before you start:** the new cases `T074-01`, `T074-02` and `T074-04` (section 6) are red on the unchanged code; `T074-03` is green before and after.
- **Set-up.**

```
cd /home/user/guidebook
bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh && python3 -c "import pydantic, jsonschema, yaml"
git fetch origin
W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1); echo "BASE=$BASE"
git switch -c task/t-074-latest-adjudication-names-the-term "$BASE"         # real execution only
sha256sum data/guidebook.db                                  # record it; this task has no migration
export SCRATCH="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/guidebook-t-074" && mkdir -p "$SCRATCH" && cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/t.db"
```
- Shell variables do not survive between tool calls: begin every later block with the `W=…; BASE=…` and `export SCRATCH=…` lines. **Real execution:** `/session-open` first. **Pilot:** no `/session-open`, stay on the given branch, stop after section 7.

## 3. The problem, in the guidebook's terms

An alias says that the phrase a source uses names one of our concepts; a rename takes a concept's name from such a phrase. Both rest on a judgment, an adjudication of the observation that records the phrase. Adjudications are appended, never edited: a second one that disagrees lands as a second row (`db.adjudicate_term`). `db._names_term`, which `add-alias` (the observation route) and `rename-term --from-observation` call, asks whether **any** adjudication of the observation names the term. An observation first judged to name a term and later judged NOT-OURS (or re-pointed at another term) still passes, so a phrase the project has since decided is not ours can become a form of the concept, or its name. What reaches the guidebook: a term shown under a name or alias its own latest judgment rejects.

**Evidence commands** (read-only on the repository; the probe writes only to a scratch copy):

```
grep -n -A5 'def _names_term' scripts/db.py
git grep -n '_names_term(' -- scripts
python3 -I - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
c = sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
LATEST = ("with latest as (select a.* from term_adjudications a where a.adjudication_id = "
          "(select max(b.adjudication_id) from term_adjudications b where b.observation_id = a.observation_id)) ")
print('observations adjudicated more than once:', c.execute("select observation_id, count(*) from term_adjudications group by 1 having count(*) > 1 order by 1").fetchall())
print('pairs some adjudication names but the latest does not:', c.execute(LATEST + "select distinct a.observation_id, a.term_id from term_adjudications a join latest l using(observation_id) where a.term_id is not null and l.term_id is not a.term_id").fetchall())
PY
cp data/guidebook.db "$SCRATCH/p.db"; mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/emptylog"
GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH="$SCRATCH/p.db" GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG="$SCRATCH/emptylog" python3 -I - <<'PY'
import os, sqlite3, sys
sys.path[:0] = ['scripts', 'scripts/research', '.']
import db
c = sqlite3.connect(os.environ['GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH'])
obs = c.execute("select observation_id from observed_terms o where not exists (select 1 from term_adjudications a where a.observation_id = o.observation_id) order by 1 limit 1").fetchone()[0]
term = c.execute("select term_id from terms order by term_id limit 1").fetchone()[0]
db.adjudicate_term(obs, 'NAMES-EXISTING', 'probe: names it', session='session_t074-probe', term_id=term)
db.adjudicate_term(obs, 'NOT-OURS', 'probe: on re-reading, not ours', session='session_t074-probe')
c = sqlite3.connect(os.environ['GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH'])
print('probe', obs, term, '_names_term ->', db._names_term(c, obs, term), '| latest outcome:', c.execute("select outcome from term_adjudications where observation_id = ? order by adjudication_id desc limit 1", (obs,)).fetchone()[0])
PY
rm -rf "$SCRATCH/p.db" "$SCRATCH/emptylog"
```

**Expected output** (2026-11-13): the function is a single `SELECT 1 … WHERE observation_id = ? AND term_id = ?`; it has two callers, `rename_term` and `add_alias`. Two observations are adjudicated twice, 88 (DEFERRED, then NAMES-EXISTING) and 97 (DEFERRED twice); **no** live pair is named by an earlier adjudication and not by the latest, so the fix changes no present act. The probe prints `_names_term -> True | latest outcome: NOT-OURS` (and `adjudicate_term`'s own `NOTE: … Writing a second row` line on stderr): the defect.

If the probe prints `False`, the defect is fixed: stop and report (section 9). If the second query prints a pair, the fix changes a present act: list the pair in the pull request and stop before merging (section 9).

## 4. The change

Order of preference, from CLAUDE.md §8: do nothing and say why; change a rule or convention; reuse what exists; delete the cause; only then add the smallest code that closes the defect. Doing nothing leaves a write path that ignores the project's own later judgment. The change is one query and two messages.

1. **`_names_term`, in `scripts/db.py`:** ask the question of the latest adjudication only.
   ```python
   def _names_term(conn, observation_id: int, term_id: str) -> bool:
       """Does the LATEST adjudication of this observation name this term?

       Adjudications are appended, never edited (adjudicate_term: a disagreeing judgment is a second
       row), so the latest one is the observation's standing judgment; an earlier one that named the
       term and was later declined or re-pointed warrants nothing. Latest = highest adjudication_id
       (the order the writer assigns; created_at is minute-resolution and can tie)."""
       row = conn.execute(
           "SELECT term_id FROM term_adjudications WHERE observation_id = ? "
           "ORDER BY adjudication_id DESC LIMIT 1", (observation_id,)).fetchone()
       return row is not None and row[0] == term_id
   ```
   **Chosen (authoring 2026-11-13): the latest adjudication governs.** It is what both refusals already tell the operator to do ("adjudicate-term … first": a new row is the remedy, so the newest row must be the one that counts), and what T-069 selects by. Rejected: refusing while the observation's adjudications disagree (a "contest" reading of `adjudicate_term`'s docstring). That reading would refuse observation 88 (DEFERRED, then NAMES-EXISTING), where nothing is contested, and it decides a question the docstring does not raise: the docstring permits a second row, it does not say the first one still warrants a write. **Chosen:** order by `adjudication_id`, not `created_at` (minute resolution: two adjudications in one minute tie).
2. **The two refusals that call it** (`grep -n -F 'no adjudication of observation' scripts/db.py` finds both): they say "no adjudication of observation N names T", which is false when an earlier one does. Make each say `the latest adjudication of observation N does not name T (none does, or a later one declined it or named another term)`, keeping the rest of each message (the remedy command) as it is. The prefix (`rename-term:` and `add-alias:`) stays.
3. **No other reader changes.** `research_batch_dod.py` R16-adjudicate deliberately counts any adjudication ("Any row answers it": `grep -n -F 'Any row answers it' scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py`): whether an observation has been judged at all is a different question. The promotion check in `db.py` (`grep -n -F "ORDER BY adjudication_id LIMIT 1\", [term_id]" scripts/db.py`) asks of a term, not of an observation: a mention. Say so in the pull request.

**What reads what this task changes:** `add-alias` (observation route) and `rename-term --from-observation`; T-069 (research) writes aliases through the first. **What wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it:** an alias or a canonical name taken from a phrase the project's latest judgment declined. **What it makes deletable:** nothing.

**Code size.** Report `git diff --shortstat "$(git merge-base HEAD "$BASE")" -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'` after `git add`.

## 5. Caller sweep

Names to sweep: `_names_term`, `no adjudication of observation`, `term_adjudications`.

**What a caller is.** A hit is a *caller* when its behaviour or its truth changes with this task: code that calls `_names_term`; a test that asserts one of the two messages' old wording (`AL02` and `N04` in `scripts/tests/test_scan_contract.py` assert only the needle `adjudicat`, which stays true: confirm); a skill or governance sentence saying an alias needs "an adjudication" naming the term (true but now incomplete: make it "the latest adjudication" where it states the rule); a view or trigger over `term_adjudications` (none on 2026-11-13: the `sqlite_master` line below). A mention stays true. Fixing a caller is in scope (CLAUDE.md rule 4). Left out: `workplan/` except `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/machines.yaml`, `references/project-standards.md`, `scripts/migrations/`, `sessions/`, `_archived/`, `audits/`, `versions/`, `transcripts/`, `scratchpad/`.

```
git grep -n -F -e "$N" -- scripts schemas .github .claude skills ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3,sys;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print([(r[0],r[1]) for r in c.execute('select type,name from sqlite_master where type in (\"view\",\"trigger\") and sql like ?',('%'+sys.argv[1]+'%',))])" "$N"
python3 -c "import yaml,sys;print([c['id'] for c in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/check-registry.yaml'))['checks'] if sys.argv[1] in str(c)])" "$N"
git grep -n -F -e "$N" -- governance architecture CLAUDE.md references workplan/pipeline-state-graph/machines.yaml ':(exclude)references/project-standards.md' ':(exclude)references/search-log'
```

## 6. Verification

**Step 1, before any edit: the before-run.**
```
CHECKS="test_scan_contract test_run_pipeline_refusals test_db_amend_writers"
for c in $CHECKS; do cmd=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys,shlex;print(shlex.join(next(x['cmd'] for x in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/check-registry.yaml'))['checks'] if x['id']==sys.argv[1])))" $c); $cmd > "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt" 2>&1; echo "$c rc=$? | $(grep -E '^ *EXAMINED:|RESULTS|FAILED|VERDICT' "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt" | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-200)"; done
```
`test_scan_contract` failed G01 and G02 on 2026-11-12, and `test_run_pipeline_refusals` X02 and X03 on 2026-11-13 (T-073's): record and carry on.

**Step 2: red before, green after** (cases `T074-01` to `T074-04` in `scripts/tests/test_scan_contract.py`, directly after the add-alias cases `AL01`…; prefix free: `git grep -c 'T074-' scripts/tests/` prints nothing). Terms: three entries of the file's own `FREE` list that no other case uses, `FREE[27:30]` (check: `grep -o 'FREE\[[0-9:]*\]' scripts/tests/test_scan_contract.py | sort -u` shows no index at or above 27; if `len(FREE) < 30`, print `SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE` for the four cases, as the T026 repair cases do). Observations: new ones made the way `OCW` is made (`attempt(observe, obs("door leaf", "PDF page 1 / T074a", "the clear width of a door leaf is measured here"), S)`, with a distinct locator suffix per observation, as T026-11 does), so their quote verifies against the fixture text. Adjudications through `adj` (`db.adjudicate_term`), never by SQL.
- `T074-01` an observation adjudicated NAMES-EXISTING to term X and then NOT-OURS: `add_alias(X, obs, "SYNONYM", S)` is refused, the message holds `latest adjudication`, and `term_aliases` gains no row. **Red before** (the old function accepts and writes the alias).
- `T074-02` the same observation: `rename_term(X, "door leaf", "fixture", S, from_observation=obs)` is refused with `latest adjudication`. **Red before.**
- `T074-03` positive control, the live shape of observation 88: an observation adjudicated DEFERRED and then NAMES-EXISTING to term Y: `add_alias(Y, obs, "SYNONYM", S)` is accepted. Green before and after.
- `T074-04` an observation adjudicated NAMES-EXISTING to Y and then NAMES-EXISTING to Z: an alias to Y is refused (**red before**), and an alias to Z is accepted.
- Seeded defect 1: order `ASC` instead of `DESC`; `T074-01` (earliest names X) and `T074-03` (earliest is DEFERRED) go red. Restore.
- Seeded defect 2: restore the old any-row query; `T074-01`, `T074-02` and `T074-04` go red. Restore.

**Fixtures** go to the copy the test makes, are labelled with the test's own session, and never reach `data/guidebook.db`.

**Step 3: after-run.** The same loop with `after-`; compare failing lines check by check; nothing new may fail. `AL02` and `N04` still pass (they assert the needle `adjudicat`).

**Step 4: the gate, once.**
```
W=$(git log --remotes --format=%H -1 -- workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline); BASE=$(git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | grep -x origin/main || git branch -r --contains "$W" --format='%(refname:short)' | head -1)
scripts/preflight.sh --base "$BASE" --explain > "$SCRATCH/gate.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E '^(RESULT|PREFLIGHT|SELFTEST)|FAIL|NOTHING-IN-SCOPE' "$SCRATCH/gate.txt"
```
Run once, in the background. If T-075 is not yet merged, run `python3 scripts/audit/research_tooling_separation.py --base "$BASE"` by hand and report it. `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` must not move.

## 7. Commit

```
git add -A . ':!transcripts' ':!*commands.jsonl'
git commit -m "governance: an alias or a rename rests on the latest adjudication of its observation [$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')]" -m "<body: the probe before and after; the live pairs query; the two messages; callers; checks with EXAMINED>" -m "<the attribution trailers your own session instructions give>"
```

## 8. What you must NOT do

- Do not add a uniqueness constraint or a refusal on a second adjudication: divergent adjudications are permitted by design (`adjudicate_term`'s docstring; CLAUDE.md §4 names the same mechanic for `add-population-match` as a refusal that must stay absent).
- Do not change `research_batch_dod.py`'s R16-adjudicate reading (section 4 item 3).
- Do not adjudicate, alias or rename anything on the canonical database (T-069's, research).
- Do not write `data/guidebook.db`. Do not run `run_checks.py --all`, `bootstrap.sh` or `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Do not push to `main`, rebase or force-push; do not subscribe to pull-request activity.

## 9. Stop conditions

Stop and report when: the probe of section 3 prints `False` (the defect is fixed); section 3's second query prints a live pair (the fix would change a present act: list it, and ask the coordinator before merging); `FREE` has fewer than 30 entries and the cases cannot run; a check green before is red after; `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` changes.

## 10. Rollback

Before merge: close the pull request, delete the branch. After merge: `git revert <merge commit>` in a new pull request.

## 11. Adversarial pass and pull request

Real execution only. `/adversarial` once; `/batch-done`; push; open the pull request last, once, against the integration base; call `unsubscribe_pr_activity` for it immediately; push nothing afterwards except a deliberate change, never `[skip ci]` on the final push.

def rename_term(term_id: str, canonical_en: str, reason: str, session: str,
                from_observation: int = None, ruling_quote: str = None,
                dry_run: bool = False):
    """Correct a term's canonical name, keeping the old one as a DEPRECATED alias.

    `amend-term` refused canonical_en since 2026-09-25 ("a vocabulary decision with
    callers, not a wording fix"), and no other verb could change it, so an answer-shaped
    or mis-chosen name was permanent (critique F5; plan section 1.2 item 6: the held ADA
    text says "turning space" and not "turning circle"). This is that vocabulary
    decision, with its warrant required:

      --from-observation N  the new name comes from a phrase a source USES, in the
                            source's own language (owner E1, 2026-11-06: a concept first
                            met outside English is named by that phrase), adjudicated to
                            THIS term, whose surface form
                            contains the new name (the 2026-09-09 rule, kept by the owner
                            on 2026-10-09: names come from observed phrases);
      --ruling-quote "..."  or from the owner's own words, quoted verbatim and found
                            exactly once in references/project-standards.md, containing
                            the new name.

    Nothing else moves: parameters, adjudications and extractions point at term_id, so the
    name is reached, never copied (rule 5). The old name lands in term_aliases as
    DEPRECATED, marked `curated` for alias_provenance_audit, and the change is recorded as
    an AMENDED line on scope_note -- the trailer amend-term already writes, so its body
    split keeps working. No other term may hold the new name, as a name or an alias.

    REFUSES: neither or both warrants; a value-bearing name (_VALUE_BEARING, as add-term);
    a quote not exactly once in the ledger or not containing the name; an observation
            warrant = f"from the owner's words in the ledger: \"{ruling_quote.strip()}\""
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        lang = _alias_language(conn, "EN")
        why = (f"curated: former canonical_en of {term_id}, renamed to {new!r} by "
               f"rename-term {warrant}. {reason}")
        held = conn.execute("SELECT alias_type, notes FROM term_aliases WHERE term_id = ? "
                            "AND alias = ? AND language = ?",
                            (term_id, old, lang)).fetchone()
        if held:
            sets = {"alias_type": "DEPRECATED",
                    "notes": dbcore.append_dated_note(held["notes"], "DEPRECATED", session,
                                                      why, stamp)}
            sets.update(_updated(conn, "term_aliases", session, stamp))
            conn.execute("UPDATE term_aliases SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                         + " WHERE term_id = ? AND alias = ? AND language = ?",
                         list(sets.values()) + [term_id, old, lang])
        else:
            arow = {"term_id": term_id, "alias": old, "language": lang,
                    "alias_type": "DEPRECATED", "notes": why}
            arow.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_aliases", session))
            conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_aliases ({','.join(arow)}) "
                         f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(arow))})", list(arow.values()))
        scope = dbcore.append_dated_note(
            term["scope_note"], _TERM_TRAILER, session,
            f"canonical_en was '{old}' (rename-term, {warrant}). {reason}", stamp)
        sets = {"canonical_en": new, "scope_note": scope}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "terms", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE terms SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE term_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [term_id])
        return {"term_id": term_id, "was": old, "now": new, "deprecated_alias": old,
                "alias_language": lang, "changed": True, "dry_run": dry_run}

                    f"--verbatim-exempt). Nothing was written.")

                    f"{obs['locator']!r}; " + (f"quote verified in {where.split(',')[0]}"
                                              if kind == "scoped" else
                                              "the observation's quote is VERBATIM-EXEMPT"))
        else:
            text = alias.strip()
            if not text:
                raise Refusal("add-alias: --alias is empty. Nothing was written.")
            # lang_jur_map is the vocabulary of research languages and their pairs; compared
            # case-insensitively, the same refusal add-term --first-form gives (T-028).

            want_j = jurisdiction.strip().upper() if jurisdiction else None

                                 "AND (? IS NULL OR upper(jurisdiction) = ?)",
                                 ((language or "").strip().upper(), want_j, want_j)).fetchall()
            if not pairs:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"add-alias: lang_jur_map holds no pair for language {language!r}"
                    + (f" and jurisdiction {jurisdiction!r}" if jurisdiction else "")
                    + ". The map is the vocabulary of research languages and the "
                      "jurisdictions each is owed in; a pair is added there, not at the form. "
                      "Nothing was written.")
            lang, jur = _alias_language(conn, language.strip()), (pairs[0][0] if jurisdiction else None)
        held = conn.execute("SELECT alias_type, observation_id, attestation, jurisdiction, "
                            "source_url, notes FROM term_aliases WHERE term_id = ? AND alias = ? "
                            "AND language = ?", (term_id, text, lang)).fetchone()
        if held and (route == "seed" or held["observation_id"] is not None
                     or held["attestation"] in dbcore.ATTESTED_FORMS):
            how = (f"attested by observation {held['observation_id']}"
                   if held["observation_id"] is not None else
                   f"attested as {held['attestation']}" + (f" at {held['source_url']}" if held["source_url"] else "")
                   if held["attestation"] in dbcore.ATTESTED_FORMS else
                   f"held as {held['attestation']}")
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id} already holds {text!r} ({lang}) as {held['alias_type']}, "
                          f"{how}. A second occurrence of an attested form waits for T-028's "
                          f"occurrence grain; a held row is never re-attested. Nothing was written.")
        if held and held["alias_type"] in ("TRANSLATION", "DEPRECATED"):
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id} holds {text!r} ({lang}) with the legacy type "
                          f"{held['alias_type']}, which no route writes for a new row. Promoting "
                          f"it would attest a back-translation or a former name as a source's "
                          f"own phrase; the legacy type is typed first (T-028/T-107). Nothing "
                          f"was written.")
        if held and held["jurisdiction"] is not None and held["jurisdiction"] != jur:
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id} holds {text!r} ({lang}) for jurisdiction "
                          f"{held['jurisdiction']!r}; the attesting source's is {jur!r}. A held "
                          f"jurisdiction is neither overwritten nor kept under a source of "
                          f"another or no jurisdiction. Nothing was written.")
        others = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT DISTINCT term_id FROM term_aliases WHERE alias = ? AND language = ? "

def insert_term(from_observation: int, canonical_en: str, rationale: str, session: str,
                definition: str = None, domain: str = None, scope_note: str = None,
                dry_run: bool = False, distinct_from: list = None):
    """Mint a term for a concept new to the vocabulary, AND adjudicate it in one act.

    The missing half of D-0173. `adjudicate-term --outcome NAMES-NEW` refuses unless the
    term already exists -- "create the term first, then adjudicate NAMES-NEW to it" --
    and nothing created one, so NAMES-NEW was an outcome the CLI documented and could
    not reach. A checker whose satisfying writer does not exist is a trap (CLAUDE.md §8).

    Term and adjudication land together because they are one judgement: *this observed
    phrase names a concept we did not hold, and here is the term for it.* Splitting them
    would permit a term with no provenance, which is the contamination the owner objected
    to on 2026-09-09 -- prior-version containers that exist before the work does.
    """
    canonical_en = (canonical_en or "").strip()
    rationale = (rationale or "").strip()
    if not canonical_en:
        raise Refusal("--canonical-en is required: a term is its name.")
    if not rationale:
        raise Refusal(
            "--rationale is required. Minting a term is an adjudication, and an "
            "adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested.")
    vb = _VALUE_BEARING_NAME.search(canonical_en)
    if vb:
        raise Refusal(
            f"--canonical-en {canonical_en!r} REFUSED: it carries a number, a comparator "
            f"or a min/max word ({vb.group(0)!r}), so it states a determination in its own name.\n"
            f"That is the defect the item layer was deleted for -- a container that "
            f"announces its answer predisposes every finding filed into it "
            f"(DR-2026-08-19 §1.1: 42 of 93 item names embedded a determination).\n"
            f"Name the PARAMETER, not the value: 'corridor width', not "
            f"'corridor width >=1200 mm'. The value belongs in the determination.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        obs = conn.execute("SELECT observation_id, surface_form, ref_id FROM observed_terms "
                           "WHERE observation_id=?", [from_observation]).fetchone()
        if obs is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"observation {from_observation}: no such observed term. A term is minted "
                f"FROM an observed phrase (db.py observe-term), never from nothing -- that "
                f"is what makes the vocabulary an output of the work rather than a "
                f"presupposition.")
        if canonical_en.casefold() not in obs["surface_form"].casefold():
            raise Refusal(
                f"--canonical-en {canonical_en!r} is not inside the observed phrase "
                f"{obs['surface_form']!r}. A name is a phrase an admitted source uses, in its "
                f"own language (owner OR-17: the model may not coin names; ruling 2026-11-06, "
                f"E1). Use the phrase as written, or a contiguous part of it. A concept first "
                f"met outside English is named by that phrase until an English-language "
                f"instrument is observed naming it.")
        clash = _name_holder(conn, canonical_en, aliases=False)
        if clash:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{canonical_en!r} is already TERM {clash['term_id']} "
                f"({clash['detail']!r}). That makes this NAMES-EXISTING, not "
                f"NAMES-NEW:\n  db.py adjudicate-term --observation-id {from_observation} "
                f"--outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {clash['term_id']} --rationale ...")
        near = [(t, h) for t, h in _near_terms(conn, canonical_en)
                if t not in set(distinct_from or [])]
        if near:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{canonical_en!r} is a near match of " +
                "; ".join(f"{t} {h!r}" for t, h in near[:5]) +
            "--rationale is required. An adjudication that does not say why cannot be "
            "contested, and being contestable is the point of splitting judgment from "
            "observation.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        obs = conn.execute("SELECT observation_id, surface_form FROM observed_terms "
                           "WHERE observation_id=?", [observation_id]).fetchone()
        if obs is None:
            raise Refusal(f"observation {observation_id}: no such observed term.")
        dbcore.check_vocab(conn, "term_adjudications", "outcome", outcome, "--outcome")
        if outcome == "NAMES-NEW":
            # NAMES-NEW lands with its term, through add-term, or it names a term that
            # already exists -- which is NAMES-EXISTING by definition. Accepted here until
            # 2026-11-06, it wrote "new" against TERM-091.
            raise Refusal(
                "--outcome NAMES-NEW is written only by `db.py add-term --from-observation "
                f"{observation_id} --canonical-en ...`, which mints the term and this "
                "adjudication together. A phrase naming a term that already exists is "
                "NAMES-EXISTING. Nothing was written.")
        names = outcome in ("NAMES-EXISTING", "NAMES-NEW")
        if names and not term_id:
            raise Refusal(
                f"--outcome {outcome} names a term, so --term-id is required. If the "
                f"phrase is not one of our concepts the outcome is NOT-OURS; if it "
                f"cannot be settled on this source alone it is DEFERRED.")
        if not names and term_id:
            raise Refusal(
                f"--outcome {outcome} declines to name a term, so --term-id must be "
                f"absent. Say NAMES-EXISTING or NAMES-NEW if it does name one.")
        if term_id and not dbcore.exists(conn, "terms", "term_id", term_id):
            raise Refusal(
                f"term_id {term_id!r} is not in `terms`. For a concept new to the "
                f"vocabulary, create the term first, then adjudicate NAMES-NEW to it.")
        row = {"observation_id": observation_id, "outcome": outcome,
               "term_id": term_id, "rationale": rationale}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_adjudications", session))
        prior = conn.execute("SELECT created_by_session FROM term_adjudications "
                             "WHERE observation_id=?", [observation_id]).fetchall()
        if prior:
            print(f"NOTE: observation {observation_id} ({obs['surface_form']!r}) already "
                  f"adjudicated by {[r[0] for r in prior]}. Writing a second row -- "
                  f"divergent judgements read as a contest, not as an error.",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        cols = ",".join(row)
        cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_adjudications ({cols}) "
                           f"VALUES ({','.join('?'*len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        return {"adjudication_id": cur.lastrowid, "outcome": outcome,
                "contested": bool(prior)}

                    --approval-ref "<a dated ledger heading naming the alias>"
